body: I wonder if this will be useful when users uses empty textures and draws their own custom grabbers, like this
This warning can be removed, since it will always trigger one of the previous warnings or both of them when `min_value` and `max_value` are `0.0`
`set_min()` does not have comment, so it's probably unnecessary.
Just like with the warning, I don't think the last check is relevant (unless you consider min/max being very close, but not equal to zero, if that can even happen).
It's not possible to set null texture, so this condition is useless.
We shouldn't call this method when `get_min()` and `get_max()` are equal zero and the previous two checks will only allow this case which can cause division by zero crash.
Eh, the new condition is basically the same.

Without this condition `!Math::is_zero_approx(get_min() - get_max())` the next line may crash 
`const double zero_ratio = get_min() / (get_min() - get_max());`, so we switch to normal fill instead.

Edit: to replace it, we will have to check if `get_min() != 0 && get_max() != 0`.

Removed it by using CMP_EPSILON instead of 0, and rebased.
`if (symmetric_fill && get_min() < -CMP_EPSILON && get_max() > CMP_EPSILON)`
